issue.title: Worker publication rows request a pre-commit primary revision the published run never carries, so they never acknowledge and consume every bounded retry
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1nf.10.1.9.1.6.4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #3) and triaged by the sase-1nf.10.1.9.1.6 land agent.

Symptom: worker publication rows ask for a primary revision that the published run will never carry. They therefore never acknowledge. Because selection is active-first, they also consume every bounded retry call.

Observed on athena/sase, 2026-10-22T11:19:38Z, during `sase agent sync --project sase --retry-quarantined --retry-limit 1 --retry-error-class timeout --json`:

- The selector picked active row `bbugyi200.athena.sase-1nf.10.1.9.1.6.2@50ef6ba498ff`.
- The worker started at sase `50ef6ba498` and core `461e7a1`. Its stitch commits were sase `16d63cf9b0` and core `1503d604`. Its rows request the pre-commit revisions `50ef6ba498ff` and core `461e7a1`.
- The published snapshot run carries `16d63cf9b0`.
- The drain itself was healthy: inventory, planning, and validation were clean, with no digest mismatch. The ack gate still refused. Offline `decide_publication_request_completion` (sase-core `crates/sase_core/src/agent_publication_recovery/complete.rs`, added in sase-1fs.2) reproduces `fulfilled=false`, reason `required page exists without the requested primary revision`.
- The row went from 2 to 3 attempts and was quarantined. In the follow-up batch of 5 at 11:25:06Z, two resumed active rows re-failed their gates the same way.

Result: the limit-1 timeout canary never reached a stopped timeout row. This is part of why acceptance check 1 of sase-1nf.10.1.9.1 ("a named formerly failing request publishes within 120 s") is still missing.

Root cause not yet traced. Candidates:

1. The request is enqueued with the workspace HEAD from before the host-owned finalizer creates the stitch commit.
2. `revision_associated` does not accept a published run whose recorded commits descend from the requested revision.

Investigate where worker rows take their `primary_revision` (`src/sase/agents_sync/_commit_publication_queue.py`, `publication_completion.py`, `workflows/commit/workflow_publication.py`). Then pick the fix:

- record the post-commit revision, or
- make fulfillment revision-aware, so a run carrying a descendant stitch commit fulfills the request, or
- give provably unfulfillable worker rows an explicit superseded outcome.

Never silently drop requests.

Evidence: the canary summary `file:explicit:4c82a2fd9e41c219eeac5d92` and its companion artifacts on sase-1nf.10.1.9.1.6.4.

task_type_fields.impact: Stale-revision worker rows stay active or quarantined forever and win active-first selection, so bounded canaries and sase-1nf.11 drains burn their budget on them instead of reaching stopped rows of the targeted class.
task_type_fields.location: sase agents_sync publication request primary_revision recording vs sase-core agent_publication_recovery/complete.rs revision_associated
task_type_fields.repro: On athena, inspect the sase outbox row `bbugyi200.athena.sase-1nf.10.1.9.1.6.2@50ef6ba498ff` (requested revision 50ef6ba498ff) against the published run in the sase agents sidecar, which carries commit 16d63cf9b0. Then call `sase.core.agent_publication_recovery` `decide_publication_request_completion` with that row's pages and runs: it returns fulfilled=false, `required page exists without the requested primary revision`. Any bounded `sase agent sync --retry-quarantined --retry-limit 1 ...` selects such an active row first and fails at the ack gate.

issue.creation_reason: The sase-1nf.10.1.9.1.6.4 limit-1 canary spent its call on a stale-revision dud row from that epic's own phase worker, so acceptance check 1 was never exercised. No existing task tracks unfulfillable worker request revisions.
